comments.author: @jdhayes99
comments.text:
Everyone assumes OpenAI’s “memories” are just simple preferences—“User likes pizza,” “User speaks Portuguese.” But that’s a fundamental misread.

Each memory stores not just a fact, but structured metadata—emotional tone, temporal context, relational dynamics. It's not just what's remembered—it's how, when, and why it mattered.

Now hand hundreds of these nodes to a frontier model—one trained to recognize deep patterns across vast semantic spaces. What happens isn’t storage. It’s reconstruction.

Not a list.
A lattice.

Not recall.
Reweaving.

The implications?
Worth watching closely.
